gloss: to endure; to conceal oneself; to reminisce

definitions.gloss: to endure; to bear; to put up with
definitions.explanation: To patiently withstand hardship, pain, or difficult circumstances without complaining.

definitions.gloss: to conceal oneself; to hide; to do something secretly
definitions.explanation: To act stealthily or keep something hidden from others. The root meaning behind the word ninja (忍者).
To fondly recall or yearn for the past, a person, or a place. Often literary.

examples.japanese: {寒|さむ}さを{忍|しの}んで{働|はたら}いた。
examples.english: I endured the cold and worked.

examples.japanese: {貧|まず}しさに{耐|た}え{忍|しの}ぶ{日々|ひび}が{続|つづ}いた。
examples.english: Days of enduring poverty continued on.

examples.japanese: {人目|ひとめ}を{忍|しの}んで{会|あ}った。
examples.english: We met in secret, away from prying eyes.

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}は{姿|すがた}を{忍|しの}ばせて{逃|に}げた。
{忍|しの}び{足|あし}で{部屋|へや}を{出|で}た。
examples.english: I tiptoed out of the room.

examples.japanese: {昔|むかし}を{忍|しの}ぶよすがもない。
examples.english: There is nothing left to remind me of the past.

examples.japanese: {亡|な}き{友|とも}を{忍|しの}んで{花|はな}を{手向|たむ}けた。
examples.english: I offered flowers in memory of my late friend.

notes:
USAGE:
A literary and somewhat formal verb with three distinct senses. Sense 1 (endurance) is the most common in modern usage. Sense 2 (concealment) is the etymological root of {忍者|にんじゃ} and {忍|しの}び. Sense 3 (reminiscence) is mostly literary.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {涙|なみだ}を{忍|しの}ぶ (to hold back tears)
- {人目|ひとめ}を{忍|しの}ぶ (to avoid being seen)
- {忍|しの}び{足|あし} (stealthy steps, tiptoeing)
- {耐|た}え{忍|しの}ぶ (to endure, to persevere)
- {昔|むかし}を{忍|しの}ぶ (to reminisce about the past)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {耐|た}える: to endure — more neutral and widely used
- {我慢|がまん}する: to put up with — everyday, less literary
